# Sources and boundaries (2026-11-19 UTC)

## A. Negative type

**Precisely what is being classified.** Conditional negative definiteness of the midpoint Jensen gap generated by the *trace-separable* functional $X\mapsto\operatorname{Tr} f(X)$, with the usual trace-one state normalisation in a fixed dimension at least three. This is an all-generators characterization, even when f is only continuous; not a claim that a new example was needed for the Shannon generator. It distinguishes Hilbertianity from metricity. For a symmetric zero-diagonal gap, Schoenberg's equivalence identifies CND with existence of a Hilbert representation as squared distances. The proof is elementary and does not assume any unverified metricity assertion.

- [Teng Zhang, arXiv:2602.08164v1, §1.2, Theorem 1.6; §9.3 Example 9.6](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08164v1#S9.SS3) already explicitly answers Virosztek's Hilbert-embedding questions for the Shannon generator: a full positive cone from dimension two, and normalized density matrices from dimension three. In particular the dimension-three negative answer itself is not new. Section 1.3 gives precisely the general trace Jensen definition, describes the qubit theorem and its limitations, and distinguishes generalized metricity. Metricity must not be confused with Hilbertianity.
- [Virosztek, Adv. Math. 380 (2021), 107595](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.aim.2021.107595), [full text](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.10447): Theorem 1 addresses Shannon's triangle inequality on positive matrices. Theorem 2, attributed to Carlen–Lieb–Seiringer, addresses qubit density matrices for operator-convex generators. This shows why a criterion in dimension three cannot be transferred to dimension two; our paper does not classify arbitrary generators on qubits.
- [Briët and Harremoës, Phys. Rev. A 79 (2009), 052311](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.79.052311) studied classical and quantum Jensen entropies and qubit/pure-state embeddings. Their §VI proposal about exponential convexity of the trace exponential is an ordinary positive-kernel question (the [TrureTuring four-qubit counterexample](https://the-omega-institute.github.io/trureturing-mdbook/Problems/briet-harremoes-2009-trace-exp-exponential-convexity.html) is to that kernel). It is not an earlier all-continuous-generator equivalence for the conditionally positive midpoint trace kernel on normalized qutrits. In particular a relation to auxiliary PD kernels is not an equivalence of the posed statements. Schoenberg's separate test using all $\exp(-sJ_f)$ uses the exponential *outside* the scalar gap.
- [Sra, LAA 616 (2021), 125–138](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.laa.2020.12.023) studies the triangle inequality for particular integral-representation classes, including quantum Shannon and Tsallis. [Sra, October 2026, Appendix B, Theorem B.1](https://hexagonmath.org/pdf/2610.00602v1) gives four-point negative type for the stated Jensen–Tsallis and Jensen–Rényi parameter ranges and shifted S-divergence mixtures; four points are not arbitrary finite families.
- [Martins et al., JMLR 10 (2009), Proposition 38](https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/papers/volume10/martins09a/martins09a.pdf) pertains to classical nonextensive kernels. [Virosztek, Jointly convex quantum Jensen divergences (2018)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0024379518301046) characterizes **joint convexity**, not CND. [Positive Definite Functions on Infinite-Dimensional Convex Cones](https://doi.org/10.1090/memo/0789) gives a general Laplace representation for positive-definite midpoint functions under a continuity hypothesis; that representation alone does not state the spectral trace-function rigidity on density matrices proved here. [Hansen, Trace functions as Laplace transforms](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0507018) treats one-dimensional positive matrix pencils; our signed tests require several directions.
- **Prior art in this repository:** [five-qutrit Jensen entropy note](https://github.com/mxym/math/tree/dd62183dbf7d0bd3296d5d213692dde0ff90aab3/research/five-qutrit-jensen-entropies) gives a single five-state family for all Jensen–Tsallis orders $0<q<2$, plus order-dependent Rényi witnesses for $0<q<1$, with its own sharper cardinality claims and a useful divided-difference test. We do not improve those cardinalities. The trace rigidity theorem does not apply to $\log\operatorname{Tr}X^q$ as if it were $\operatorname{Tr} f(X)$. [Fidelity scalar kernels](https://github.com/mxym/math/tree/dd62183dbf7d0bd3296d5d213692dde0ff90aab3/research/fidelity-matrix-scalar-kernels) deals with a function of pairwise fidelity and ordinary Gram positivity, not trace Jensen gaps.
- Search included names and variants (quantum symmetric Jensen f-divergences, generated trace entropy, negative type, Hilbert and Hilbertian, matrix/Jensen–Bregman kernels, exponentially convex trace functions, Laplace representation, Schoenberg, Schatten, trace inverse). As of this search no earlier fixed-dimension classification with the same all-continuous quantifier was located. This is neither proof of novelty nor a named open question in those precise words. No outside peer review.

## B. Exact reciprocal triangle

**Statement checked.** [Teng Zhang, “Metric Properties: From S-Divergence to Quantum Jensen Divergence”, arXiv:2602.08164v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2602.08164v1), Theorem 1.9 and Corollaries 1.10 and 10.3. The first assumes a non-affine operator-convex generator, finite and continuous at zero, and a faithful tracial state; the last explicitly covers trace-one density matrices in every dimension. The generator in the proof is defined on the *whole* positive half-line, not only on the spectral interval, and meets those assumptions. Using a normalized trace scales all squared gaps by the same positive constant. At the date checked the [arXiv record](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.08164) listed one version. No conclusion is drawn about future revisions, author intent or the separate Shannon results.

**Compare these positive results.**
- [Virosztek, 2021, Theorems 1 and 2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1910.10447): Shannon metric on the full positive cone; and, by the Carlen–Lieb–Seiringer argument, Hilbertianity on *trace-one qubits* for all operator-convex generators, including reciprocals. The latter proof actually uses a reciprocal basis. Our three qutrits are normalized, but their upper two-by-two blocks do **not** have identical trace. The scalar completion (and its explicitly counted gap) is essential for this comparison. Simultaneous diagonalization cannot be used, since the off-diagonal endpoint blocks do not commute.
- [Sra, LAA 616 (2021), 125–138, Theorems 3.1/3.6 & Eqs. (3.3)/(3.8)](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10327602) imposes specific positive shifted-logarithm representations. Our generator is excluded, not a counterexample to Sra. Indeed in the convex sign convention each shifted negative-log term gives $x^2 f''(x)=x^2/(t+x)^2$, nondecreasing for $t\ge 0$; affine terms vanish and nonnegative mixtures preserve monotonicity. The same test applies to (3.8) with shape $t^2x^2/(1+tx)^2$. In contrast $x^2 f''(x)=2\cdot79^2x^2/(1+79x)^3$ is positive and tends to zero at infinity. [Sra's 2026 Theorem B.1](https://hexagonmath.org/pdf/2610.00602v1) also concerns specific mixtures, and particular parameter families; no contradiction.
- Teng Zhang's Theorem 1.6/Example 9.6 already established the failure of *Hilbertianity* for the Shannon Jensen gap. It does not establish failure of Shannon triangle, and neither do we. The existing [five-qutrit project](https://github.com/mxym/math/tree/dd62183dbf7d0bd3296d5d213692dde0ff90aab3/research/five-qutrit-jensen-entropies) concerns negative type of Shannon/Tsallis/Rényi entropies and includes prior four-point positive results for its specific generators. The present calculation uses a different generator and only three states. The main, separate classification of CND for continuous trace generators by itself would **not** disprove metricity.

**Additional overlap in quantum Hellinger divergences.** Writing $P=(I+79X)^{-1}, Q=(I+79Y)^{-1}$ identifies our quantity exactly with $\operatorname{Tr}[(P+Q)/2-2(P^{-1}+Q^{-1})^{-1}]$, the arithmetic–harmonic difference. This belongs to the established generalized Hellinger class of [Pitrik and Virosztek, Quantum Hellinger distances revisited](https://arxiv.org/abs/1903.10455); defining that divergence is not a contribution. [Jeong and Kim, ELA 41 (2025), 236–247](https://journals.uwyo.edu/index.php/ela/article/download/8883/6985/24217) study arithmetic–harmonic quantum divergences and barycenters. [Bhatia–Gaubert–Jain, 2019, §2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1901.01378) give examples in which the square root of the arithmetic–geometric difference fails the triangle inequality, for the Kubo–Ando geometric and log-Euclidean means. Neither mean is the harmonic mean. A quantum triangular discrimination can also mean a *measured* supremum or other quantum chi-square expressions [Liu](https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.01952); commuting formulas alone do not identify these objects. Note that applying the inverse map also changes traces, so ordinary trace-one constraints on the reciprocal inputs and the original states are different.

**Limits of search.** Searched the paper title, arXiv identifier, author name, operator-convex Jensen metric, reciprocal/resolvent/trace inverse, arithmetic–harmonic/Hellinger differences, matrix/quantum triangular discrimination, nonmetricity and triangle failure; checked public theorem collections (including [TrureTuring](https://www.trureturing.org/conjectures.html?lang=en)) for closely matching exact statements. An equivalent earlier result under a change of variables remains possible. No priority claim is made. No outside peer review.

**Important qualitative implication.** [Matsumoto's proof of Prop. 18](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1006.0302) plus [the maximal-divergence formula and straight-line continuity, Thm. 6.1 and Eq. (9.5)](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1311.4722) already imply existence after a short transfer argument: see the accompanying [derivation](PRIOR-IMPLICATION.md). These papers do not need to literally state the later conjectural assertion in order to constitute material prior art. The diagnostic value here is a three-state all-rational triangle for a specified generator, not a proposed first discovery of abstract existence.
